fields.consequence: A systematic offset on every sounding. It does not average out and it does not look like noise — the whole survey is displaced, consistently, and looks perfectly plausible until somebody overlays a second one.

fields.consequence: The coverage ribbon is painted on the wrong side of the track, so the map shows ground that was never surveyed as surveyed.
fields.label: Side the sonar looks

fields.consequence: Endurance is arithmetic on this. Wrong here is a confident wrong number telling somebody they have forty minutes left.
fields.label: Battery capacity

fields.consequence: Endurance, again. Everything that is not propulsion.
fields.label: Hotel load

fields.consequence: Dominates the link's useful range: the two-ray term goes as the product of the two antenna heights, so this is worth more than any transmit power we are allowed to use.
fields.label: Boat antenna height above water

fields.consequence: Without it the link panel cannot show range or bearing from the sector, so a link about to fail looks exactly like one that is fine.
fields.label: Shore station latitude

fields.consequence: As above; the two are captured together.
fields.label: Shore station longitude

fields.consequence: The number that turns 'the link dropped' into 'the link is going to drop'. Without it nobody can see the boat working towards the edge of the sector.
fields.label: Shore station bearing

fields.consequence: Sets where the close-in multipath nulls fall, and the far cliff.
fields.label: Tripod height above water

fields.consequence: Decides whether the link's multipath nulls exist at all. On a glassy morning the link drops out and comes back at a fixed range, which looks like a fault and is not one.
fields.label: Sea state

fields.consequence: Three decibels of range per doubling, against twice the throughput. A real trade and worth making deliberately.
fields.label: Radio channel width

fields.consequence: The datum every recorded metre is relative to. Move it and the whole mission moves with it, silently.
fields.label: Local origin latitude

fields.consequence: As above; the two are derived together.
fields.label: Local origin longitude

fields.consequence: Too short and the bottom is outside the window. Obvious within a minute of pinging, which is why this is not in the group that ruins a survey quietly.
fields.label: Sonar range

fields.consequence: Too low and the returns are weak; visible on the sonar panel.
fields.label: Sonar gain

tiers.blurb: How the boat is built. Measured once, properly, and then left alone — these do not change between missions and they never go stale.
tiers.label: Vessel

tiers.blurb: Where you are today. The tripod, the water, the depth you expect. These are re-checked every time the boat goes in, and the page says how old each one is.
